title: Proto-cuneiform barley and field account from Jemdet Nasr (MSVO 1, 10)
source: OIM A02515 photograph, transliteration and English translation via CDLI (P005077)
description: Proto-cuneiform barley and field account from Jemdet Nasr: a clay tablet from Jemdet Nasr of about 3200-3000 BCE, among the earliest written documents, with CDLI's transliteration and English.
introduction:
This clay tablet (OIM A02515, Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures West Asia & North Africa Museum, Chicago, Illinois, USA) is a proto-cuneiform document of the Uruk III period, about 3200-3000 BCE, from Jemdet Nasr (CDLI catalogues the provenience as uncertain, attributed to Jemdet Nasr). It is a short account of 150 units of barley for a field of 10 bur, recorded by the pigsty accountant.

Proto-cuneiform is the earliest stage of cuneiform writing, used for bookkeeping in southern Mesopotamia. It records numbers in several counting systems (shown in the transliteration as signs N01, N14, N34 and so on) together with signs for goods, offices and places. It does not yet write full sentences, so the English is an interpretation of the entries rather than a translation of connected language.

The sections follow the faces and columns of the tablet. The transliteration and the English are CDLI's, line by line with the same line numbers.
translator_notes: Transliteration: CDLI ATF (proto-cuneiform). Numerals are written as counts of numeral signs, e.g. 4(N14) = four N14 signs; ~a, ~b mark sign variants; [ ] broken, # damaged; sz is shown as š.
English: CDLI's line-by-line translation (#tr.en lines of the ATF).

CDLI notes: reverse, line 1: calculation: 150N1 ÷ 10 = 15N1 barley per bur3; reverse, line 1: following later tradition and assuming this is a seeding account, it would support an identification of the base unit in grain metrology, N1, with ca. 20-25 liters
